errors.text: The starting material is incorrectly described as powder produced from a cast alloy rather than nominally equimolar high-purity elemental Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti powders.

The proposed 1100–1200 °C SPS window is substantially above the target 900–1000 °C regime and conflicts with the intended boundary near 1000 °C, beyond which grain coarsening or phase decomposition becomes a concern.
The 10–20 h milling duration does not reconstruct the target 1–6 h window and may increase contamination, phase evolution, and over-milling risks.
The asserted displacement-derived strain-rate window of 10^-3 to 10^-2 s^-1 is unsupported by the cited evidence and is not equivalent to the target SPS displacement constraints.
The supporting papers concern compositionally different refractory HEAs and do not validate the claimed FCC/BCC stability window for CoCrFeNiTi.
